title: LIVE Lyon Open Final | Taylor Fritz’s fleeting ATP Finals hopes intact as Lorenzo Musetti eyes first title in four years
text:
Lyon Open Final | Lorenzo Musetti wins first ATP title in four years against Taylor Fritz Tournaments ▼ Newsletter FAQ Calendars ▼ Players ▼ Originals ▼ Live Scores Lyon Open Final | Lorenzo Musetti wins first ATP title in four years against Taylor Fritz
 ATP by Lucas Michael Sunday, 25 October 2026 at 16:08 Follow us on Google! 0 Before today, Lorenzo Musetti had not won an ATP title since
October 2022. Finally, that well-documented drought has come to an end. He won
the Lyon Open with a 6-3, 6-4 victory over Taylor Fritz whose ATP Finals chances
have taken another dent. ARTICLE_IN_2
 --> 
 After a tremendous 2025, albeit without silverware, 2026 has
been a nightmare in comparison for Musetti. Just one final before this at the
start of the year in Hong Kong, he has plummeted outside the top 20 in the
world and has been stripped of any consistency thanks to constant injury woes. Finally, he is able to leave a tennis tournament with a
smile on his face and a trophy by his side. Four long years have come and gone,
and finally he has something to show for his hard work. 
 In contrast, it was a fifth ATP final in 2026 for Fritz, a
second indoors. He managed to win just one of them on home soil at the DC Open.
He has also endured injury issues which have left chances of returning to the
ATP Finals almost in tatters. A title triumph would have rewarded him with crucial
points as he attempts a last-gasp charge to Turin, but he could not produce the
level on court needed to prevail over Musetti. The 24-year-old fired himself out in front early and kept
that advantage as he won the first set. He remained on top throughout, keeping
it cool when it mattered to get over the line. A massive burden was shaken from
his shoulders, with glory in France confirmed. Lorenzo Musetti is finally back in the winners circle Title drought over as Musetti downs Fritz
 Musetti got off to the brighter start. He was pushed in the
first set, but Fritz was not able to create any break points. The unforced errors
started to ramp up, and Musetti capitalised. He won eight points in a row to
break and hold to love, taking an ominous 3-0 lead. ARTICLE_IN_2
 --> 
 Fritz finally got on the board in this final but had much
work to do. Musetti restored his three-game buffer, and that would be the final
time in the first set that he dropped points on serve. He was producing a high level, and Fritz was simply unable
to react and match it. All he could do was force Musetti to serve it out, and a
second consecutive hold to love did the job. Musetti moved a set to the good,
and within touching distance of a long-awaited title triumph. Read also

His task was made even simpler when a third break point in
the second set was converted. After a brace of holds, Musetti again made
inroads on the Americans' serve and eventually took his chance. Fritz attempted to muster up a response, but still no break
points were created. The equation was simple for Musetti. Just keep holding his
serve, and he would win the title. Fritz forced him to get the job done on his
own terms. He took his first championship point before falling to the floor, hugely
